biography:
Jaime Levy, a name synonymous with audacious speed in the Puma P052 camp, hails from the vibrant favelas of Rio de Janeiro. His racing journey began not on asphalt, but on the treacherous, winding dirt tracks that crisscrossed the hills surrounding his home. As a kid, he scavenged parts to build makeshift go-karts, honing his skills in daring races against older, more experienced rivals. One sweltering afternoon, a chance encounter with a talent scout at a local karting event changed everything. Blown away by Jaime's raw talent and fearless overtaking maneuvers, the scout offered him a spot in a regional racing academy. 

Jaime quickly rose through the ranks, showcasing an uncanny ability to master any vehicle he piloted. He is a showman, and he knows it, but it comes from a place of genuine love for the sport. A defining moment came during the Brazilian National Championship, where, despite a mechanical failure in the penultimate lap, he managed to coax his sputtering car across the finish line, securing a crucial championship point. His flamboyant celebrations afterwards cemented his reputation as a charismatic and sometimes controversial figure. Currently, Jaime is focused on establishing himself as a force to be reckoned with in the Puma P052 series, aiming to translate his raw talent into consistent podium finishes and championship contention. 

While his driving skill is not considered the best among drivers, he certainly has a knack for getting the car to the line. He is known to push the car harder than most drivers would dare, often leading to spectacular results or spectacular failures. But it is his flair for showmanship that keeps the fans coming back for more. He loves to play the role of the villain, and that role is what he will play to the best of his ability.
drivingStyle: Jaime's driving style is a blend of controlled aggression and raw intuition. He's known for his late braking and daring overtaking maneuvers, often diving down the inside of corners where others wouldn't dare. He is not known for his tyre management, as he usually burns through them quickly. He relies on his natural feel for the car to adapt to changing track conditions, and while he can be prone to mistakes under pressure, his aggressive approach often yields unexpected results.

careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the Puma P052 Series race at Interlagos in 2051, costing him valuable championship points and enduring relentless teasing from rivals.
